chunks: That which the Sheikh — may Allah the Exalted support him — informed me of: he said, Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Abdallah (AS), who said:

A man said to 'Ali ibn al-Husayn — peace of Allah be upon him: 'Where do strangers perform wudu?' He replied: 'One should avoid the banks of rivers, the thoroughfares, beneath fruit-bearing trees, and the places of cursing.' It was said to him: 'And where are the places of cursing?' He said: 'The doorways of houses.'

key_terms.اَلنَّافِذَةَ: passable, traversable (of roads — denoting public thoroughfares)
key_terms.اَلْغُرَبَاءُ: strangers, travelers, those away from home
key_terms.مَوَاضِعَ اَللَّعْنِ: places of cursing, locations where one incurs the curses of others
key_terms.يَتَّقِي: should avoid, should be wary of, should guard against

ai.seo_question: What four places did Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) forbid for answering nature's call and performing wudu?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) transmits that a man asked Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin (AS) where travelers and strangers should attend to their bodily needs (and perform wudu). The Imam enumerated four forbidden locations — riverbanks, public thoroughfares, beneath fruit-bearing trees, and 'places of cursing' — and when pressed, identified the last category as the doorways of houses, where relieving oneself would invite the curses of the residents.
